preregistration.justification: The groove root has a finite radius (a problem fact), so the continuum stress is bounded and the peak has a finite limit; no singular exponent applies. The projected-dilatation (P1) peak changed 2->3: -38.2%, 3->4: -5.1%, 4->5: -11.0%: the last change is larger than the one before, so the sequence does not yet contract. The displacement-only peak approaches it: the gap L2: 1.476, L3: 0.629, L4: 0.283, L5: 0.151 shrinks every level. Without a contracting sequence no extrapolation or rate is possible; one more level is the cheapest test that can decide between a converging and a non-converging peak.
preregistration.hypothesis: H1: the P1 peak is converging and the L4->L5 drop is pre-asymptotic: at level 6 the change contracts and the formulations keep approaching.

prediction.text: |P1(L6)/P1(L5) - 1| < 0.110 (the L4->L5 change) AND |disp(L6) - P1(L6)| < 0.151 (the L5 gap)

preregistration.if_confirmed: the peak may become certifiable: at least one more level is needed for three contracting changes; still reported as not verified until then
preregistration.if_refuted: report the groove peak and the stress-concentration factor as not verifiable with the present discretizations; stop refining
preregistration.confidence: low-medium: theory says bounded, but the last change grew

outcome.conclusion: the peak may become certifiable: at least one more level is needed for three contracting changes; still reported as not verified until then
